text: The Gordon Heights Fire Department is a volunteer fire department located in and serving the hamlets of Gordon Heights, Medford, Middle Island, and Yaphank in the Town of Brookhaven, Suffolk County, on Long Island, New York, United States. It is the sole department within the Gordon Heights Fire District. Prior to its establishment in 1947, there were no fire services in the community, which was founded in 1927; neighboring departments did not have a responsibility to provide protection. After a fire destroyed a local church, the Civic Association initiated efforts to form a community fire department, which was officially incorporated shortly thereafter. By 1948, the department had acquired its first fire truck. When the fire house became too small, residents advocated for the creation of a fire district to generate taxes and fund expansion, leading to petitions submitted to the Town Board. The first commissioners were appointed in 1952–53, followed by an election one year later. The Gordon Heights Fire District has faced criticism in recent years, with some residents claiming it has the highest tax rates on Long Island, a situation partly due to the district's lack of a commercial tax base. Opponents also point out its small size, serving about 900 homes compared to surrounding districts that serve between 4,400 and 8,700 households and have lower tax burdens. Supporters of the 60-member district highlight its status as the first Black fire department in New York State and its ability to offer services not available to larger departments, such as assisting elderly residents with snow plowing during winter. In 2006, an attempt to dissolve the district was rejected by the Town of Brookhaven because the petition was improperly formatted. A second dissolution petition was filed on December 31, 2008, but both attempts failed, and the department remains active as of 2021.
